newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to donate over 60,000 tonnes of rice as aid.
newsitem.headline: Japan to donate over 60,000 tonnes of rice as aid.

text.p: Japan will donate more than 60,000 tonnes of rice to seven countries in Africa, to Laos and to Haiti, officials of the Agriculture Ministry said on Tuesday.
The Japanese government had decided to donate the rice from its domestic rice stocks as aid, they said, adding that this was an attempt to reduce excessive domestic grain stocks.

Japan's Agriculture Ministry has estimated that domestic rice stocks at the end of October 1996 -- the end of the crop year -- stood at three million tonnes, almost double the 1.61 million tonnes of a year ago.
Good harvests in the past two years have swollen stocks in grain warehouses across the country. A stock level of 1.5 million tonnes is considered desirable throughout the year.

"At this stage, we have no clear idea whether the food aid should be from domestic rice or foreign rice. We'll work out the point soon through discussions with those countries," Agriculture Minister Takao Fujimoto told reporters.

Earlier this month former Agriculture Minister Ichizo Ohara proposed sending foreign rice Japan is obliged to import under world trade accords back overseas. Major rice exporters, such as Australia, said this would be against the spirit of the GATT Uruguay Round agreements.

Japan currently spends about 13 billion yen annually on food aid programmes under its Official Development Assistance, particularly for poor countries in Africa and Asia, according to the Foreign Ministry.
The government provides cash-strapped countries with funds to import food such as Thai rice.
Ministry officials said the African countries expected to receive rice aid from Japan were Senegal, Tanzania, Togo, Benin, Madagascar, Mauritania and Mozambique.
